pr.title: Link a summary file to its project and branch, and set inline notes apart
pr.head: d8bb1d641df3246aa6545d4585a0f4bfeec2538c

summary: A summary page, like this one, walks a reviewer through a pull request's diff one file card at a time. Each card's header holds the file's path, its line counts, a few links, and a Reviewed box. The header linked to the file in the pull request's diff, labelled PR, and to the file at the commit the summary describes, labelled file. A reader who wanted the plan a file belongs to had to find it in the site's Projects section by hand.
This pull request gives each header three links:

• Diff opens the file in the pull request's diff on GitHub. It is the old PR link under a clearer name.
  • File opens the file on the pull request's head branch, pr.headRef, so it shows the branch's current version. Once the site build finds the pull request merged or closed, it links the head commit instead, because GitHub deletes a merged branch in this repository and keeps the commit. A summary with no headRef also links the head commit.
  • Project opens the site's page for the project whose folder holds the file. It appears only when the site has a page for that project.
To learn whether a pull request merged, the site build now asks GitHub for its state in the same request that fetches its reviews, one GraphQL query in place of the REST reviews call.

A review note under a diff line also changes shape. Each note is now its own table row, with its tag, such as context or concern, in the line-number gutter and its text where the code starts. Reviewed sits 6px further from the header links.
The review of the first head found that the File link broke once a pull request merged. This head fixes that, and the review of this head is clean.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Summary: the JSON a review writes for a pull request, which the site renders as a page like this one.
  • Site build: project site build, which the repository's Pages workflow runs on each deploy. It reads every stored summary and writes each page's data.json.
  • Project: a folder under docs/projects/ with its own lowercase readme.md. Projects nest, and a project's folder can also hold supplemental files.
  • pr.head: the commit a summary describes. pr.headRef: the pull request's head branch, which project summary init records. pr.state: open, merged, or closed, as the last site build found it.

cards.title: What the review ran at this head
cards.html:
• npm ci, npm run check, and npm run build in site/: no lint findings, and the build leaves site/assets/summary.js unchanged.
  • All 502 Python tests under Python 3.12, including the new open, merged, closed, and unknown-state cases.
  • summary.pr_status run live: merged for #197 and open for #203, with the same 8 reviews for #197 as the REST endpoint it replaces.
  • project check, both claude plugin validate commands, and git diff --check.

groups.title: The site build finds each file's project and records the state
groups.kicker: Where the Project link's target comes from
intro: The site build already worked out which projects a pull request touches, so a review page could list them and each project page could list its reviews. project_linker does that work: for each changed file, it finds the deepest project folder that holds the file, among the projects the site has pages for.
The change keeps that search and also writes its answer onto the file, as a project object with the project's name, title, and site URL. The renderer reads that object to draw the Project link.

files.note: project_linker sets project on each changed file it can place. build_summaries takes the renamed status_lookup and writes pr.state onto each page.

checks.text: The candidate folders come from the projects in the checkout the build runs in, sorted longest path first, so the first match is the deepest project. A project the pull request adds has no page until the site deploys from a checkout that has it, so its files get no link on an open pull request.

The build writes data.json after this mutation: build_summaries calls the linker on the payload, then serializes the same payload. test_a_file_belongs_to_the_deepest_project_the_site_has reads project back from data.json and passed at this head.
Every stored head of a pull request gets the same state, so an older head's page also switches to commit links once the pull request merges.

groups.title: The site build learns each pull request's state
groups.kicker: One GraphQL query returns the state and the reviews
intro: On each deploy, the site build asks GitHub for every summarized pull request's reviews, to show whether its head was reviewed. The File link also needs to know whether the pull request has merged or closed, so the build asks for the state in the same request.

summary.pr_status replaces summary.pr_reviews. It sends one GraphQL query for the pull request's state and its reviews, a page of 100 reviews at a time, and returns both. The build writes the state onto each page as pr.state. When GitHub cannot be asked, a page gets neither a state nor a review status, and its File links stay on the branch.

checks.text: The state is read when the site deploys. A merge that touches the files the site workflow watches starts a deploy, and so does each summary publish, so a page can keep branch links for a while after a merge.

files.note: Replaces pr_reviews with pr_status, a paginated GraphQL query for the state and the submitted reviews.

checks.text: Run against GitHub at this head, pr_status returned merged for #197 and open for #203. For #197 it returned the same 8 submitted reviews as the REST endpoint, with the same OWNER association that review_statuses checks.
An answer with no state raises SummaryError, which build_checkout turns into no state and no review status.

files.note: build_checkout passes pr_status as the build's status_lookup, and still answers None when GitHub cannot be asked.

groups.title: The renderer draws the new header and note rows
groups.kicker: The TypeScript that draws each file card, and its compiled copy
intro: renderSummary in site/src/summary.ts draws the whole summary page in the browser from data.json. The file card header is one string of HTML; this change relabels the first link, points the second at the branch or the head commit, and adds the third.

A note under a diff line is now a table row of its own: a ngut cell holds the note's tag across the line-number columns, and an nte cell holds its text, with a Handled checkbox for a concern. A diff with one line-number column, such as a new file's, is marked oneside so the smaller tag fits.
The repository commits the compiled JavaScript beside the TypeScript, because every deploy and every CLI install reads the site's assets from a Git tree. site/assets/summary.js is that compiled copy.

files.note: Types the new project field on a file, and the optional headRef and state on pr.
Adds blobUrl for the File link, relabels the links, draws Project when the file has one, and draws each note under a line as its own row.

checks.text: blobUrl uses the head commit when pr.state is merged or closed, and the branch otherwise, including when the build could not learn the state. test_the_file_link_follows_the_branch_until_the_pull_request_merges_or_closes covers all four cases and passed at this head.
Each segment of the branch and of the path goes through encodeURIComponent on its own, so the slashes between segments stay, and a # in a name becomes %23 instead of starting a URL fragment.
The tag cell spans sides columns, one or two line-number columns, and the text cell takes the code column. Several notes on one line make several rows.
Project links within the site, so it opens in the same tab, unlike Diff and File, which open GitHub in a new one. esc escapes both the URL and the title.

A concern's checkbox now finds its row as well as a list item, so checking it dims a note under a line through tr.noterow.checked. The open-concern count reads every .note-box in the file, so it still counts these.

files.note: Compiled from site/src/summary.ts. The review rebuilt it with npm run build and got the committed file back unchanged.
Adds margin-left: 6px to Reviewed, styles the note rows' gutter tag and text cells, and drops the .inotes rules that nothing renders any more.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: The header tests, and the two documents that describe the links
intro: FileHeaderTests builds one summary through project site build for a diff that touches a project's readme, a supplemental file in that project, a nested project's readme, a readme for a project the site lacks, and src/app#1.py outside every project. Four of its tests run the compiled renderSummary under node and check the header links, the File link for each pull request state, and the note rows; they skip where node is missing.
PrStatusTests checks that pr_status reads the state and every page of reviews from one query. The CLI reference and the summary format guide describe the links.

files.note: Adds FileHeaderTests and rendered_summary, which cuts renderSummary out of the compiled file and runs it under node with a stub document.
Replaces the REST reviews test with PrStatusTests, including an answer with no state.
Describes the three header links, and the head-commit link once the build finds the pull request merged or closed.
Says when the File link uses pr.headRef and when it uses pr.head.
